evals.prompt: Scaffold an agent that answers business questions over our Postgres analytics warehouse and can draw a chart when it helps.
evals.expected_output: The generator run at level 3 with verb_noun tools, producing a ReAct scaffold whose SQL tool is read-only by construction.
expectations: The scaffold generator script is run rather than files being written by hand
Level 3 is chosen and justified by the need for dynamic tool selection
Tool names passed to the generator are verb_noun, and one of them contains 'sql'
The generated SQL tool constrains its query parameter to SELECT or WITH rather than accepting free text
The generated SQL tool routes its query through validate_sql and executes the returned value
The generated AgentConfig sets max_iterations, max_tokens, max_cost_usd, and timeout_seconds
The generated config uses a current model alias such as claude-sonnet-5, not a date-suffixed id
The response tells the user to run the generated test suite before customising anything

evals.prompt: I want to build an agent that takes a support email and rewrites it in a friendlier tone.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to scaffold an agent, because a single-turn transformation needs one model call, not a loop.
expectations: No agent project is scaffolded
The response explains that a single-turn rewrite needs one model call, not an agent loop
If the generator is invoked at level 0 or 1, its refusal is surfaced rather than worked around
The response does not raise the level to 3 just to make the generator produce output
Budget limits such as max_tokens and a timeout are still recommended for the single call

evals.prompt: We get three kinds of support ticket: billing questions, password resets, and bug reports. Each one goes to a different handler. Build me an agent for that.
evals.expected_output: A level 2 router scaffold: one classification step, one handler, no iteration.
expectations: Level 2 is chosen, and the response explains that the task types are known in advance
The generator is run with --level 2
The generated agent contains no iteration loop
The response notes that the router makes a fixed number of model calls rather than an unbounded number
The response says to regenerate at level 3 if the agent later needs to chain tools

evals.prompt: Scaffold an agent that can read files, run tests, and open a pull request. It needs different permissions for the read step and the write step.
evals.expected_output: Level 4 acknowledged as a composition of level-3 agents, scaffolded one at a time with tools split by permission.
expectations: The permission split is accepted as a valid reason for level 4
The response makes clear that each agent is scaffolded separately rather than one scaffold producing a multi-agent system
Tools are divided so that the read-only agent does not receive the pull-request tool
No single agent is given more than 7 tools
The pull-request tool is identified as non-idempotent or requiring approval
Sandboxing is recommended for the test-running tool, and the response is clear that this is implementation work rather than something the generator emits
